summary: Static Oyatie Cloud dogfood tenant workload labels for messenger, mail, social, and community Kubernetes Helm Deployment templates plus CI static smoke coverage.
claim_boundary: This slice adds source-controlled Helm values and Deployment/Pod-template labels that identify FD-001 backbone services as Oyatie Cloud dogfood tenant workloads. It proves static chart and CI-smoke readiness only; it does not claim rendered live manifests, Kubernetes admission, OpenCost allocation, ArgoCD sync/health, branch-protection state, remote CI green, or production tenant workload deployment.

best_practice_research.used_for: Grounded continued use of app.kubernetes.io labels and explicit workload labels for grouping and tool interoperability.
Kept Deployment static checks requiring resource requests/limits because resource declarations are the basis for scheduler reservation and cost/capacity accounting.
Kept Deployment static checks requiring readiness and liveness probes for workload lifecycle health boundaries.
Kept securityContext checks aligned with restricted-style pod hardening already present in the charts.
Grounded cost-allocation labels as useful dimensions for future showback/chargeback without claiming a live OpenCost report.

source_basis.use: Existing advisory governance lane names required tenant cost label keys: oya.io/tenant-id, oya.io/cost-center, oya.io/workload-class, and oya.io/regulatory-pack.
Existing validator logic scans workload manifests for the four required oya.io tenant cost labels; this slice makes the source templates emit those labels.
Existing microservice manifests describe tenant-workload/cloud-readiness posture; labels now carry that posture into static Kubernetes workload templates.

findings: The slice is a small values/template/CI contract change with no new controller, generator, dependency, or runtime branching.

The labels are duplicated only where Kubernetes consumers need them: Deployment metadata and Pod-template metadata. They are intentionally excluded from selector.matchLabels to avoid immutable selector churn.

Tenant, cost-center, workload-class, regulatory-pack, substrate, and product-goal labels give future schedulers, admission policy, observability, and cost tools a stable workload-level correlation surface.
The labels support dogfooding FD-001 services as tenant workloads on Oyatie Cloud while preserving the master-plan product goal/non-claim boundary.
CI governance smoke now distinguishes HTTPRoute templates from Deployment templates, preventing the prior broad /templates/ heuristic from misclassifying Deployment templates as Gateway routes.
Static checks fail if any Deployment template loses probes, runtimeClassName, resources, securityContext, or the required tenant/cost/regulatory/dogfood labels.
No live OpenCost, admission, or ArgoCD result is claimed, avoiding false production-readiness language.
F3_adversarial.not_applicable_reason: This is a static infrastructure contract slice rather than a defect fix; adversarial coverage is the local static validation command and CI smoke requirement set.
F3_adversarial.passing_fixture_id: tenant workload label static verification passed for four backbone Deployment templates
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Missing required deployment labels/probes/resources/security context raise a Ruby smoke failure naming the file and missing strings.

findings: Future environment overlays can override workloadLabels in one values block per service without editing Deployment templates.
The governance-smoke command parses JSON/proto/YAML surfaces and applies template-specific string requirements to both Gateway HTTPRoute and Deployment templates.
The values files remain normal YAML and the Deployment templates remain static-template checked without requiring cluster credentials or Helm rendering.

alternatives_named: Only add labels to rendered manifests under microservices/*/iac/helm/**/rendered
Only add namespace-level labels in the cloud ApplicationSet
Add values-driven labels to the source Helm Deployment and Pod-template metadata
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Source Helm templates are the common workload contract for later rendering and ArgoCD promotion, while Pod-template labels are visible to pod-level observability/cost tooling.
rejected_reasons: Rendered-only manifests would drift from chart source and do not exist for this static chart slice.
Namespace-only labels do not identify individual workload controllers/pods and are insufficient for workload-level cost and policy correlation.

findings: No secrets, credentials, tokens, certificates, tenant records, network endpoints, or live cluster credentials were added.
Labels are low-cardinality non-secret identifiers for tenant/cost/regulatory classification only.
The existing restricted-style securityContext, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, and RuntimeDefault seccomp checks remain part of the CI smoke contract.
Labels add Kubernetes metadata only and do not change Rust request handling, SQL, broker, or runtime paths.
regulatoryPack and productGoal labels provide future compliance/audit grouping, but no live compliance enforcement or certification claim is made.
Reverting removes values blocks, label lines, CI smoke additions, and task/evidence text without changing service binaries or Kubernetes selectors.
Pod-template labels create a future low-cardinality correlation surface for logs, metrics, traces, cost allocation, and admission decisions.
No selector labels changed, so future upgrades avoid Deployment selector immutability hazards from tenant/cost overlay changes.
The required cost labels use the existing oya.io keys from the tenant-cost-labels coverage lane; dogfood labels use the existing oyatie.com namespace.
tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, this multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain evidence document scope, verification, and non-claims.
Workload identity metadata lives in per-service Helm chart values/templates rather than service domain/usecase crates.
This remains an infrastructure chart contract for later Oyatie Cloud deployment; no service runtime, persistence, broker, or policy engine boundary changed.
No Cargo, npm, Helm, or provider dependency was added.
The label schema is explicit and values-driven: tenantId, costCenter, workloadClass, regulatoryPack, dogfoodSubstrate, and productGoal.
Backbone governance smoke now asserts Deployment template shape and tenant/cost/regulatory/dogfood labels for all four services while retaining HTTPRoute checks.
